title: Shadow of the Dynasty
next_chapter_hook: Just as Chen Ji was deciding his next move, an unusual sound of footsteps suddenly rang outside the inn—it was not the aura of a cultivator, but a fluctuation of the "Dragon Qi" unique to the Dynasty.

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng's figure flickered out like a dying candle, but his final words exploded like thunder in Chen Ji's Mental Sea. He knelt before the Tianji Record Fragment, the surrounding Spiritual Energy chaotic as boiling water, the veins on his temples bulging.

"The Heavenly Secret's Eye is merely a piece..."

He repeated this sentence, his voice terrifyingly hoarse. For three years since obtaining the Tianji Record, he believed he had seen through the chess game of this world—the friction between the three great sects, the Demonic Path invasion, the opening of the Ancient Forbidden Land—all were pieces on his board to dominate the world. But now he realized, the board he thought he understood was merely a speck of dust on an even grander game.

Chen Ji rose abruptly, his sleeves creating a gust of wind. He shut his eyes, the Tianji Record Fragment warming in his palm—the Foresight Ability stirred within. After merely three breaths of hesitation, he forcefully suppressed that impulse.

"Cannot look... not now."

He gritted his teeth. The Heavenly Fate Value had only ninety-three points remaining; every glimpse of the future cost precious life tokens. Moreover, Mo Xiansheng's words made him realize a terrifying possibility—if the Heavenly Secret's Eye itself was a manipulated piece, then how much of the future he saw through the Tianji Record was a genuine chess game?

dialogue.content:
"So from the start, we were all being led by the nose."

Chen Ji suddenly laughed, the sound carrying three parts of madness and seven parts of bone-deep coldness. The mask of a cowardly Servant Disciple shattered completely in this moment, revealing the terrifyingly savage face beneath.

text.content:
He took a deep breath, forcing himself to remain composed. His thoughts cut like a blade, peeling back layers of information from Mo Xiansheng's words.

Dynasty.

This term wasn't entirely foreign to him. Among ordinary mortals, cultivators were revered as lofty immortals; within cultivator legends, the Dynasty represented an even more ancient and mysterious existence. Legends spoke of an epoch when the Dynasty ruled over everything—both mortals and cultivators were its subjects. Later, for reasons unknown, the Dynasty vanished into the mists, leaving only the tale of "The Shepherds" behind.

Chen Ji had once dismissed these as mere ancient myths, stories crafted by mortals to comfort themselves. Yet Mo Xiansheng's direct confirmation now proved that the cultivation sects were nothing more than the Dynasty's herding dogs.

The grand narrative of three major sects, the righteous versus demonic paths, the cosmic struggle between good and evil—everything he'd considered a monumental chess match was, in the Dynasty's view, merely sheep squabbling over grass in a pasture.

dialogue.content:
"Fascinating... truly fascinating."

Chen Ji murmured to himself, his tone devoid of much anger, instead brimming with an almost manic excitement. His eyes gleamed dangerously in the darkness, the thrill of a hunter encountering a far more formidable prey.

"Since the Heavenly Secret's Eye is merely a piece, then the Dynasty is but one Chess Player among others. Is there an even higher existence above the Chess Players?"

text.content:
He slowly sat back onto the meditation cushion, the Tianji Record Fragment automatically flying into his sleeve. His thoughts blazed like lightning, countless ideas colliding in his mind.

Mo Xiansheng said that the true master behind the Heavenly Secret's Eye was a certain prince within the Dynasty. What did this mean? It meant that prince had been maneuvering for at least several centuries—perhaps longer. The fates of generations of prophets, the fragmentation of the Tianji Record, and even his own "rise"—were all these within that prince's calculations?

text.content:
Chen Ji closed his eyes and began reorganizing all his arrangements over the past three years in his mind. How many of those moves he once considered brilliant were truly his own will, and how many were guided by that prince?

This realization made his spine go cold, yet also made him clearer-headed.

choices.description: Since the chessboard has already changed, rather than waiting passively, proactively seek clues left by the Dynasty, seize the initiative in the larger chess game.

choices.visible_reward: Might gain Dynasty intelligence in advance, even find alliance possibilities

text.content:
Chen Ji stood up and walked to the window. Moonlight fell upon his face, revealing eyes as deep as an abyss.

"Since we're going to play chess, let's play the biggest game of all." He murmured to himself, "The Dynasty wants to treat the cultivation world as a pasture—I'll show them, sheep can also grow fangs."

dialogue.content:
He took out a black jade talisman, the communication token Ye Qing had left before parting. The talisman's surface was ice-cold, with faint demonic energy flowing through it.

"The Demonic Path mist can conceal the Tianji Record's aura... If the Imperial Court is truly monitoring everything, then Ye Qing's abilities may be more valuable than imagined.

Chen Ji injected a wisp of spiritual energy into the talisman, and a flash of dark red light disappeared. The message had been sent, now all that remained was to wait.

text.content:
Just at this moment, the Tianji Record Fragment suddenly vibrated violently.

Chen Ji's expression changed slightly, and he quickly retrieved the fragment. On the yellowed surface, the originally blurry runes were slowly transforming, faintly outlining a pattern never seen before—it was an eye, but different from the tyranny of the Heavenly Dao's Eye, this eye carried an ancient and authoritative aura, as if standing above all things.

At the bottom of the fragment, a line of small characters was appearing: "Imperial Court · Dragon Depths Pavilion".

Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply.

Dragon Depths Pavilion. He had never seen this name in any classic text, but instinct told him this must be some key faction under the Imperial Court. Was the Tianji Record actively showing this information coincidental or divinely guided?

He dared not act rashly, only deeply carving those five characters into his mind. Mo Xiansheng had said, the more complete the Tianji Record, the stronger the fatal backlash of fate. Now that the fragment was actively revealing Imperial Court information—what did that mean? Was the Tianji Record itself guiding him toward a grander chess game, or had that prince finally taken notice of him?

text.content:
Chen Ji pondered for a moment, then finally made his decision. He spread out the fragment, formed seals with both hands, and began consuming Heavenly Fate Value to peer into the future. Three breaths later, a blurry image emerged before his eyes—

It was a palace floating above the clouds, and before it stood a young man in a golden robe. The young man's features were unclear, but those eyes... were identical to the eye pattern newly appearing on the fragment.

"Found you." The golden-robed figure in the vision seemed to sense the peering, a meaningful smile curving his lips.

Chen Ji abruptly opened his eyes, cold sweat beading on his forehead. The foresight was forcibly interrupted, but he had already seen the most critical information—the Imperial Court was watching him.

text.content:
Chen Ji tucked the fragment into his sleeve, the fervor in his eyes gradually subsiding, replaced by his usual composure and calculation.

Though the Imperial Court was vast, with his current strength, rash contact would be like throwing an egg against a rock. Better to continue playing the fool while hiding his true abilities, accumulating strength within the sect's chess game. When his wings are fully developed, then he could play against that golden-robed prince.

It's just that... thinking of that golden-robed man's smile, a chill rose in Chen Ji's heart. That wasn't the ordinary arrogance of a prince, but the playful look of a hunter who has spotted prey.

Night deepened, and Chen Ji sat alone in his room, a pot of coarse wine placed on the table before him. He rarely drank in his daily life, but tonight, he needed something to calm his turbulent emotions.\n\nMo Xiansheng's words were like a key, opening a door he had never imagined. Beyond that door lay an even broader and more dangerous world. The rise and fall of the three major sects were merely ripples in a pond, and the Imperial Court was the leviathan lurking in the deep sea.

He suddenly remembered that rainy night three years ago. Back then, he was still a newly arrived servant disciple of the Tianqing Sect, who had accidentally found that torn page of the Tianji Record in the waste elixir room. At that time, he thought it was a tremendous stroke of luck, a beginning of changing his fate.

How laughable.

He tilted his head and drained the wine in his cup, the spicy liquid burning his throat. The so-called stroke of luck was nothing more than a piece on someone else's chessboard. And his three years of struggle and scheming, perhaps, was merely an entertaining show in the eyes of that prince.

However, Chen Ji had never been someone content to accept his fate.

He set down his wine cup, the gloom in his eyes gradually fading, replaced by an almost cold determination. So what if he was a piece? So what if he was being manipulated? Since he could fight his way through the struggle among the three major sects, since he could repeatedly frustrate the schemes of the Heavenly Dao's Eye, then facing the Imperial Court, he would not sit still and wait for death either.

"You say the Heavenly Dao's Eye is a piece, and I am the piece of a piece." he said quietly, his voice carrying a chilling coldness, "But don't forget—a piece can also turn the tables."

text.content:
Chen Ji's aura instantly became long and steady, exactly like a worthless disciple in sound sleep. Yet his divine sense spread quietly like a spider's web, capturing every movement around him.

Outside the window, an almost imperceptible intention swept over him. That intention was cold and majestic, carrying a lofty scrutiny—that was the disregard of a superior for an inferior, yet also with a trace of subtle inquiry.

"Interesting." An aged voice rang in his Mental Sea, "Indeed as the rumors say, utterly mediocre. But to be mediocre to this degree is rather thought-provoking."

The intention receded like the tide, yet Chen Ji was drenched in cold sweat. The owner of that voice was at least a Nascent Soul stage expert!

text.content:
Chen Ji pushed open the door, and the night wind carried a bone-piercing chill that slammed against him. The courtyard was empty, yet he knew the visitor lurked in the shadows.

"Since you're here, why skulk in the shadows?" His voice was not loud, yet it clearly spread in all directions.

After several breaths of silence, a figure slowly manifested from the void. It was an elderly man with white hair, wearing a Gray Robe embroidered with dragon patterns, with no Spiritual Energy fluctuations around him, appearing as an ordinary mortal elder.

But Chen Ji knew that someone capable of quietly infiltrating past the Tianqing Sect's protective mountain formation was no ordinary person.

The elder approached slowly, each step falling on the rhythm of Chen Ji's heartbeat. Those murky old eyes contained the vicissitudes of someone who had seen through the ways of the world and undeniable authority.

"Servant Disciple Chen Ji?" The elder's voice was hoarse and low, "Indeed as the intelligence said, an absolute waste."

He stopped three zhang away from Chen Ji, his gaze like a blade, as if wanting to dissect Chen Ji open to look.

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji lowered his eyes, hiding all his sharpness within the shell of mediocrity. He slightly hunched his back, his hands awkwardly rubbing the corner of his robe, looking completely like someone whose courage had been shattered.

"Elder... elder must have mistaken me?" His voice trembled slightly, "This junior is merely a servant, not worth an elder's personal visit..."

Before he finished speaking, the elder suddenly raised his hand, and an invisible force pinned Chen Ji in place.

text.content:
"Waste?" The elder sneered, "A waste that has attracted the attention of Longyuan Pavilion—this is the first time in a thousand years."

He circled around Chen Ji, like examining an interesting collectible.

"Tianqing Sect Servant Disciple, entered the sect three years ago with no progress in cultivation, daily only knows sweeping the courtyard, carrying water and chopping firewood. However..." the elder's tone shifted, "In these three years, those who had contact with you—dead, crippled, or missing—total seventeen people. The deaths of your several senior brothers remain unsolved cases to this day. Tell me, is this coincidence?"

Chen Ji's heart plummeted.

Seventeen. He never imagined the empire's investigation of him had reached such meticulous levels. Among those people were villains who tried to harm him, greedy scoundrels coveting the 'treasure' on him, and innocent souls who had inadvertently witnessed his secrets. He thought he had handled things cleanly enough, yet he hadn't expected everything to be observed.

But what chilled him even more was the elder's next words—

"Longyuan Pavilion is very interested in you." The elder bent down, his murky old eyes staring directly at Chen Ji, "Especially... that thing on you."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's body stiffened, his pupils constricting sharply. He knew what the other party meant—the Tianji Record.

Yet, contrary to the elder's expectations, the fear on this 'waste's' face actually vanished in an instant without a trace. Replacing it was a calm that made one's spine go cold.

"What does the elder want?" Chen Ji's voice no longer trembled, instead carrying an eerie calm, "Want to take it? Or want me to serve Longyuan Pavilion?"

The elder hesitated slightly, then burst into laughter.

"Interesting, truly interesting!"

text.content:
The laughter stopped abruptly, the elder's gaze becoming sharp as a blade.

"Neither." he said, "Longyuan Pavilion is merely interested in you, that's all. As for what you choose to do—whether to continue being a waste, or break free from the chessboard to become a chess player... that's your own affair."

He took out an ancient-looking token from his sleeve and gently placed it on the stone table before Chen Ji.

"This is the Longyuan Token. With it, you gain the qualification to enter the empire's field of vision. If one day you become strong enough to want to break the game, it will guide your direction."

Chen Ji did not reach for the token, merely watching the elder before him silently.

"There's no free lunch in this world." he said, his voice terrifyingly calm, "What does Longyuan Pavilion want from giving me this token?"

The elder nodded approvingly.

"Smart." He turned and walked into the darkness, his voice drifting over, "Longyuan Pavilion only wants you to remember one thing—the one behind the Heavenly Eye will soon take notice of you. At that time, whether you choose to become his chess piece or choose to cooperate with us... is entirely up to you."

As his words fell, the elder's figure had vanished into the night.

The night wind blew across the courtyard, carrying a desolate chill.
